comparison: Both evaluate study design and sample composition (C12, C13, C20, C21) and scRNA-seq methods (C22-C31). OpenEval finds all claims supported with adequate documentation. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study design but criticize 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' though they don't challenge the basic findings.

OpenEval evaluates scRNA-seq methods and cell identification (C22-C31) as well-documented and supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge these methods but express concern about 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' suggesting the approach may be overly descriptive rather than analytically rigorous.

Both evaluate immune infiltration and tumor heterogeneity findings (C14, C32-C34). OpenEval finds these claims supported by scRNA-seq data and consistent with expected biology. Peer reviewers do not challenge these compositional findings and acknowledge they align with the study's comparative design.

Both evaluate metabolic reprogramming claims (C15, C35-C38). OpenEval finds these supported by GSVA analysis but notes validation at protein/functional level would be beneficial. Peer reviewers express stronger concern about 'insufficient statistical support' and 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' rating the evidence as uncertain rather than adequately robust.

Both evaluate tumor cell malignancy and pseudotime analysis (C39-C45). OpenEval finds these supported by CNV and trajectory analysis but notes validation is needed. Peer reviewers express concern about 'insufficient statistical support' and 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' suggesting these findings lack adequate validation.

Both evaluate metabolically active tumor subclusters (C46-C51). OpenEval finds these supported by SCENIC and metabolic pathway analysis, though notes functional validation would strengthen findings. Peer reviewers criticize 'insufficient statistical support' and 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' rating evidence as uncertain.

Both evaluate stromal cell findings including myofibroblast absence after NCT (C52, C53, C55-C58). OpenEval finds these supported by stromal analysis though notes small sample size limits generalizability. Peer reviewers find these inadequately supported, citing 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis' and insufficient statistical rigor.

Both evaluate metabolically active fibroblast subclusters (C59-C63). OpenEval finds these well-documented by clustering and SCENIC analysis but notes mechanistic validation needed. Peer reviewers express concern about 'insufficient statistical support' and 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis,' rating evidence as uncertain.

Both evaluate macrophage metabolic reprogramming (C64-C73). OpenEval finds these supported at transcriptional level though notes functional validation would strengthen conclusions. Both evaluate macrophage classification and plasticity (C74-C81). Both evaluate functional characterization of macrophage subtypes (C18, C87-C91). OpenEval finds strong evidence from differential expression, ELISA, and in vivo experiments. Peer reviewers cite 'insufficient statistical support' and 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis.'

Peer reviewers apply criticism of 'lengthy descriptive clustering-type analysis' and 'insufficient statistical support' to these B cell characterizations.
